cases.translation: The smile might have seemed crude.
cases.explain: Улыбка is the grammatical subject of показалась бы (would have seemed), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: еще раз поцеловав ее руку выше ___.
cases.translation: Kissing her hand once more above the glove.
cases.explain: The preposition выше (above) governs the genitive case.

cases.translation: Stepan Arkadyevich went to his sister.
cases.explain: The preposition к (toward) governs the dative case.
Руку is the direct object of the transitive verb поцеловал (kissed), so it is accusative.

cases.sentence: Степан Аркадьевич, покачивая ___, сказал это с сочувственным выражением лица.
cases.translation: Stepan Arkadyevich, shaking his head, said this with a sympathetic expression.
cases.explain: The verb покачивать (to shake/nod) takes its object in the instrumental case, as in покачивая головой (shaking one's head).

cases.translation: Stepan Arkadyevich met her in the doorway.
cases.explain: The preposition в (in) indicating location governs the prepositional case, here the plural form дверях (in the doorway).

reading.ru: Еще Бетси не успела выйти из залы, как Степан Аркадьевич, только что приехавший от Елисеева, где были получены свежие устрицы, встретил ее в дверях.
reading.question: Where had Stepan Arkadyevich just come from when he met Betsy in the doorway?
options: Yeliseyev's, where fresh oysters had just arrived
reading.correct: Yeliseyev's, where fresh oysters had just arrived
reading.explain: The text says he had just come from Yeliseyev's, where fresh oysters had been received.

reading.ru: «Встреча на минуту, потому что я уезжаю», — сказала Бетси, улыбаясь и надевая перчатку.
reading.question: Why did Betsy say their meeting would only be brief?
options: Because she was late for a ball
Because Karenin was waiting for her
reading.explain: Betsy says «Встреча на минуту, потому что я уезжаю» — the meeting is brief because she is leaving.

reading.ru: Я не только устраиваю свои, но и чужие семейные дела», — сказал он с значительным выражением лица.
reading.question: What did Stepan Arkadyevich claim to be doing with a significant expression on his face?
options: Arranging not only his own but other people's family affairs
Writing a novel about his family
reading.correct: Arranging not only his own but other people's family affairs
reading.explain: He says he arranges не только свои, но и чужие семейные дела — not only his own but other people's family affairs.

reading.ru: «Он уморит ее», — сказала Бетси значительным шепотом.
reading.question: What did Betsy whisper meaningfully about Karenin and Anna?
options: That he would be the death of her
That he would forgive her fully
That he would leave for Tashkent
reading.correct: That he would be the death of her
reading.explain: Betsy whispers «Он уморит ее» — 'He will be the death of her.'

reading.question: How does Betsy describe Anna's condition?
options: She is wasting away more and more
She is getting stronger every day
reading.correct: She is wasting away more and more
reading.explain: Betsy says of Anna, Она тает и тает — she is wasting away, fading more and more.

reading.ru: Он не понимает, что она одна из тех женщин, которые не могут шутить своими чувствами.
reading.question: What does Betsy say Karenin fails to understand about Anna?
options: That she is one of those women who cannot trifle with their feelings
That she wants a lavish party
That she has always disliked Vronsky
That she wishes to move abroad
reading.correct: That she is one of those women who cannot trifle with their feelings
reading.explain: Betsy says he does not understand that Anna is one of those women who cannot joke with (trifle with) their feelings.

reading.ru: Меня сделали камергером, ну, надо было благодарить, но главное, надо устроить это».
reading.question: What honor had Stepan Arkadyevich just received, according to what he tells Betsy?
options: He was made a court chamberlain
He was awarded a medal for bravery
reading.correct: He was made a court chamberlain
reading.explain: He says Меня сделали камергером — he was made a chamberlain, though he says the main thing is to arrange 'this' (Anna's situation).

reading.question: In what state did Stepan Arkadyevich find his sister Anna?
reading.explain: The text says Он застал ее в слезах — he found her in tears.

reading.ru: «Я слыхала, что женщины любят людей даже за их пороки», вдруг начала Анна.
reading.question: What did Anna suddenly say about women and men's vices?
options: That she had heard women love men even for their vices
That she had never loved anyone with vices
That men always hide their vices
reading.correct: That she had heard women love men even for their vices
reading.explain: Anna begins by saying she has heard that women love men даже за их пороки — even for their vices.

reading.ru: Я ненавижу его за его великодушие, и мне ничего не остается, кроме...
reading.question: What does Anna say she hates her husband for?
reading.explain: Anna says Я ненавижу его за его великодушие — she hates him for his magnanimity.

reading.ru: Я как натянутая струна, которая должна лопнуть».
reading.question: How does Anna describe her own state to Stepan Arkadyevich?
options: Like a taut string that must snap
Like a bird about to fly free
Like a ship safely in harbor
reading.correct: Like a taut string that must snap
reading.explain: Anna says Я как натянутая струна, которая должна лопнуть — she is like a taut string that must break.

reading.ru: Ты вышла замуж за человека, который на двадцать лет старше тебя.
reading.question: What does Stepan Arkadyevich remind Anna about her husband's age?
options: That she married a man twenty years older than her
That her husband was younger than her
That her husband was the same age as her
That her husband's age was unknown
reading.correct: That she married a man twenty years older than her
reading.explain: Stepan Arkadyevich says Ты вышла замуж за человека, который на двадцать лет старше тебя — she married a man twenty years her senior.

reading.question: What solution does Stepan Arkadyevich present as untying all the problems?
reading.explain: He argues Тогда как развод развязывает все — whereas divorce unties (resolves) everything.
